# astro-css-module-types

An Astro integration that types each CSS module's class names, so typos like `styles.tile` (for `styles.title`) fail `tsc` and `astro check`.

Astro's `astro/client` types declare every `*.module.css` import as a record of any string keys.
This integration writes a `.d.ts` file next to each CSS module that lists the class names Vite actually exports for it.
TypeScript uses that file instead of the loose `*.module.css` declaration:

```ts
// Generated by astro-css-module-types from Text.module.css.
declare const styles: {
	readonly text: string;
	readonly toneMuted: string;
};

export default styles;
```

The files are generated by `astro sync`, `astro check`, `astro build`, and `astro dev`, which also updates them as CSS modules are added, changed, and deleted.
Each of those also deletes generated files whose CSS modules no longer exist.

## Usage

```ts
// astro.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";

import { cssModuleTypes } from "./integrations/astro-css-module-types";

export default defineConfig({
	integrations: [cssModuleTypes()],
});
```

The generated files aren't meant to be committed.
Add them to your `.gitignore`, which Prettier also reads, along with any other CSS module extensions you use, such as `*.module.scss.d.ts`:

```gitignore
*.module.css.d.ts
```

If ESLint lints `.d.ts` files in your project, ignore them there too:

```ts
// eslint.config.ts
import { globalIgnores } from "eslint/config";

export default [globalIgnores(["**/*.module.css.d.ts"])];
```

Run `astro sync` before running `tsc` on its own, as you would for Astro's other generated types, such as with a `"tsc": "astro sync && tsc"` script.
Without a generated file, an import falls back to the loose `*.module.css` declaration, and a stale one can keep a deleted CSS module's imports type checking.

## Options

### `directories`

Directories to look for CSS modules in, relative to the project root.
Defaults to Astro's `srcDir`.
Directories whose names start with `.` and `node_modules` directories are skipped.

```ts
cssModuleTypes({ directories: ["src", "packages/ui/src"] });
```

## How It Works

Class names come from Vite's own `preprocessCSS()`, given the project's `vite.css` and `vite.resolve` options.
That means the same CSS modules options (such as `localsConvention`), PostCSS config, and preprocessors as Vite's real imports.
CSS options that Vite plugins add, and changes that Vite plugins make to CSS before Vite compiles it, aren't seen.
Files with any extension Vite treats as a CSS module are supported, such as `.module.scss`, if their preprocessor is installed.

CSS modules in `src/pages` (or your `srcDir`'s `pages`) get an error instead of types, because Astro would treat their `.d.ts` files as routes.
Ones in a directory whose name starts with `_`, which Astro doesn't make routes from, are fine.

The integration never changes how Vite builds CSS, and only writes or deletes `.d.ts` files that start with its `// Generated by astro-css-module-types` comment.
If a hand-written `.d.ts` is already next to a CSS module, it reports an error instead of replacing it.

Types only include the default export, as `astro/client` declares, not Vite's named exports for each class name.
